hints: Notice power output is $150 \text{ kW} = 150 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$ but fuel use is $20$ litres per hour, so the time units do not yet match.
Recall power input is energy supplied per second, so first find fuel energy per hour from $20$ litres per hour $\times$ $40 \text{ MJ}$ per litre.
To change $800 \text{ MJ}$ per hour into watts ($\text{J s}^{-1}$), divide by $3600 = 60 \times 60$, which means $60 \times 60$ must move to the top of the output-over-input fraction.
walkthrough: Identify the given data: power output $= 150 \text{ kW} = 150 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$, and fuel supplies $20$ litres every hour with $40 \times 10^6 \text{ J}$ per litre.
Calculate fuel energy supplied per hour: $E = 20 \times 40 \times 10^6 \text{ J}$ in $1$ hour.
Convert power input to watts using $P = E/t$ with $1 \text{ hour} = 60 \times 60 \text{ s}$: $P_{in} = 20 \times 40 \times 10^6 / (60 \times 60)$ in $\text{W}$.
Form the efficiency ratio: $P_{out}/P_{in} = 150 \times 10^3$ divided by $[20 \times 40 \times 10^6 / (60 \times 60)]$.
Rearrange the division by a fraction to multiplication: $P_{out}/P_{in} = 150 \times 10^3 \times 60 \times 60 / (20 \times 40 \times 10^6)$ with no unit mismatch.

A.explanation: This divides by $60 \times 60$ instead of multiplying, giving power input in $\text{J h}^{-2}$ rather than $\text{J s}^{-1}$.

B.explanation: This correctly converts $150 \text{ kW}$ to $150 \times 10^3 \text{ W}$ and divides by fuel energy per second $20 \times 40 \times 10^6 / (60 \times 60)$.

C.explanation: This multiplies power output by fuel energy per hour, which gives units of $\text{W} \times \text{J}$ and is not a power ratio.

D.explanation: This uses $40 \times 10^3$ for the fuel energy content instead of $40 \text{ MJ} = 40 \times 10^6 \text{ J}$ per litre.
